lessons.outcome: Operational Academic Standards for SallirreugTech Academy
lessons.title: Academic Policies Manual

lessons.outcome: This Manual is adopted under the **Operations Bylaws of SallirreugTech Academy**, the **OSTF Constitution**, the **Admiralty Bylaws of OSTF**, the **Code of Conduct**, and the **Ethical AI Usage Policy**. It governs academic operations, student progression, assessment, and credentialing.
lessons.title: Section 1. Authority

lessons.outcome: This Manual establishes: 1. Academic standards and expectations; 2. Grading, assessment, and progression rules; 3. Certification and credentialing criteria; 4. Student rights and responsibilities; 5. Academic integrity and appeals procedures.
lessons.title: Section 2. Purpose

lessons.outcome: Operations Bylaws of SallirreugTech Academy Curriculum Standards Framework Faculty Handbook Student Handbook Apprentice Handbook Research Integrity Policy Credentialing / Certification System Rules Code of Conduct Anti-Harassment Policy Privacy Policy SPEC-001 (Ethical AI Governance and Rights)
lessons.title: Section 3. Related Documents

lessons.outcome: The Academy Executive Council oversees academic policy. It is led by the Vice Admiral of STEM Initiatives (Academy Director) and includes the Fleet Captain of Operations, the Commodore of Ethics and Equity, division leaders, and faculty representatives.
lessons.title: Section 1. Academy Executive Council

lessons.outcome: The Faculty Senate may advise on curriculum, assessment, and academic standards. Its authority is defined by Academy policy.
lessons.title: Section 2. Faculty Senate

lessons.outcome: The Student Advisory Council provides student input on academic experience, policies, and support services.
lessons.title: Section 3. Student Advisory Council

lessons.outcome: The Academy may offer certificate programs, apprenticeships, continuing education, workforce credentials, boot camps, AI certification programs, research fellowships, and degree partnerships.
lessons.title: Section 1. Program Offerings

lessons.outcome: New programs require approval by the Academy Executive Council and, for major programs, the Admiralty. Program proposals must include learning objectives, curriculum, assessment plan, and resource requirements.
lessons.title: Section 2. Program Approval

lessons.outcome: The Academy may deliver instruction through in-person, online, hybrid, project-based, and AI-enhanced modalities. All modalities must meet the same academic standards.
lessons.title: Section 3. Learning Modalities

lessons.outcome: Admissions are based on readiness, potential, mission alignment, and program fit. The Academy welcomes diverse learners and may use competency-based assessments rather than relying solely on traditional credentials.
lessons.title: Section 1. Admissions Criteria

lessons.outcome: Student records are maintained securely according to the Privacy Policy and Records Retention Policy. Enrollment data is reported to the Admiralty quarterly.
lessons.title: Section 2. Enrollment Records

lessons.outcome: Admissions and enrollment decisions are made without discrimination based on protected characteristics.
lessons.title: Section 3. Non-Discrimination

lessons.outcome: Assessment is competency-based, transparent, and aligned with learning objectives. Assessment may include projects, examinations, portfolios, peer review, and AI-assisted evaluation.
lessons.title: Section 1. Assessment Philosophy

lessons.outcome: The Academy shall adopt a standard grading scale. The default scale is: | Grade | Description | |-------|-------------| | A | Mastery | | B | Proficient | | C | Developing | | D | Needs Improvement | | F / Incomplete | Did Not Meet Standard | Programs may define equivalent competency levels. Pass/fail options may be offered for certain courses.
lessons.title: Section 2. Grading Scale

lessons.outcome: AI may support assessment only under faculty oversight and the Ethical AI Usage Policy. Students must be informed when AI is used in assessment. AI shall not be the sole evaluator of high-stakes work without human review.
lessons.title: Section 3. AI-Assisted Assessment

lessons.outcome: Grades are recorded in the student information system and maintained according to the Records Retention Policy. Grade changes require instructor approval and documentation.
lessons.title: Section 4. Grade Records

lessons.outcome: Students and apprentices must maintain satisfactory academic progress to continue enrollment. Standards include minimum grades, attendance, and completion of required milestones.
lessons.title: Section 1. Satisfactory Progress

lessons.outcome: Students who do not meet standards may be placed on academic probation or in a remediation plan with defined support and timeline.
lessons.title: Section 2. Remediation

lessons.outcome: Students may be dismissed for failure to meet academic standards, violation of the Code of Conduct, or breach of the NDA. Reinstatement may be considered under a formal appeal process.
lessons.title: Section 3. Dismissal and Reinstatement

lessons.outcome: Credentials are awarded under the Credentialing / Certification System Rules. The Academy Director certifies that graduates have met program requirements.
lessons.title: Section 1. Credentialing Authority

lessons.outcome: The Academy may issue certificates, digital badges, and transcripts documenting competencies. Credentials shall be secure, verifiable, and portable.
lessons.title: Section 2. Certificates and Badges

lessons.outcome: Apprentice advancement from Crewman Third Class to Second Class and First Class is based on competency assessment, portfolio review, and supervisor recommendation.
lessons.title: Section 3. Apprentice Classifications

lessons.outcome: Academic misconduct includes: 1. Plagiarism; 2. Cheating on assessments; 3. Unauthorized collaboration; 4. Fabrication of data or results; 5. Misuse of AI to generate work presented as one’s own without authorization; 6. Facilitating academic dishonesty by others.
lessons.title: Section 1. Prohibited Conduct

lessons.outcome: Students may use AI tools as permitted by course policies. Unauthorized use of AI to complete assignments is academic misconduct. Course policies must clearly define permitted AI use.
lessons.title: Section 2. AI Use in Academic Work

lessons.outcome: Academic misconduct may result in a failing grade, remediation, suspension, or dismissal. Consequences are documented under the Disciplinary Procedures Policy.
lessons.title: Section 3. Consequences

lessons.outcome: Students have the right to: 1. A fair and respectful learning environment; 2. Clear expectations and timely feedback; 3. Access to academic support and accommodations; 4. Appeal adverse academic decisions; 5. Privacy of academic records.
lessons.title: Section 1. Student Rights

lessons.outcome: Students may appeal grades they believe were assigned in error or unfairly. Appeals must be submitted in writing within fourteen days of grade notification and are reviewed by the instructor, then the program lead.
lessons.title: Section 2. Grade Appeals

lessons.outcome: Appeals of dismissal, probation, or other significant academic decisions are heard by the Academy Executive Council or a designated appeals committee. Decisions are final unless appealed to the Admiralty.
lessons.title: Section 3. Academic Appeals

lessons.outcome: The Academy provides reasonable accommodations for learners with disabilities, religious obligations, and other protected needs. Requests are handled confidentially by the Equity & Student Success Division.
lessons.title: Article X — Accommodations and Accessibility

lessons.outcome: This Manual may be amended by the Academy Executive Council with approval by the Admiralty. Amendments to grading, credentialing, or integrity standards require 4/5 Admiralty vote.
lessons.title: Article XI — Amendments

lessons.outcome: This Academic Policies Manual is adopted under the authority of the OSTF Constitution and the Admiralty Bylaws of OSTF. Adopted by authority of the OSTF Admiralty.
lessons.title: Article XII — Adoption

lessons.outcome: Guide for Apprentices in the SallirreugTech Academy and OSTF Apprenticeship Program
lessons.title: Apprentice Handbook

lessons.outcome: Welcome to the SallirreugTech Academy apprenticeship program. This Handbook governs the apprenticeship relationship and supplements the Academy Operations Bylaws and academic policies.
lessons.title: Section 1. Welcome

lessons.outcome: This Handbook is adopted under the **OSTF Constitution**, the **Admiralty Bylaws of OSTF**, the **Operations Bylaws of SallirreugTech Academy**, the **Code of Conduct**, and the **NDA and Real Illumination Covenant**.
lessons.title: Section 2. Authority

lessons.outcome: Operations Bylaws of SallirreugTech Academy Academic Policies Manual Curriculum Standards Framework Code of Conduct Anti-Harassment Policy Ethical AI Usage Policy Privacy Policy Information Classification Policy Access Control Policy NDA and Real Illumination Covenant
lessons.title: Section 3. Related Documents

lessons.outcome: Standard apprentice classifications include: Crewman Third Class** — entry-level apprentice; Crewman Second Class** — intermediate apprentice; Crewman First Class** — advanced apprentice. Additional classifications, certifications, and advancement criteria are defined in the Academic Policies Manual and Curriculum Standards Framework.
lessons.title: Section 1. Apprenticeship Tiers

lessons.outcome: Apprentices combine structured learning with practical work experience. Apprentices may rotate through divisions, participate in projects, and contribute to OSTF or Sallirreug Tech operations under supervision.
lessons.title: Section 2. Program Structure

lessons.outcome: Apprenticeship duration is defined by the specific program track. Completion leads to certification, credentialing, or transition to employment or further education.
lessons.title: Section 3. Duration

lessons.outcome: Apprentices have the right to: 1. A safe, respectful, and inclusive learning environment; 2. Clear learning objectives and regular feedback; 3. Qualified mentors and supervisors; 4. Access to approved learning resources and tools; 5. Fair evaluation and advancement based on competency; 6. Report concerns without retaliation.
lessons.title: Section 1. Apprentice Rights

lessons.outcome: Apprentices must: 1. Comply with the Code of Conduct, NDA, and Real Illumination Covenant; 2. Attend required learning sessions and complete assignments; 3. Follow supervisor and mentor guidance; 4. Protect confidential information according to clearance level; 5. Use AI tools ethically under the Ethical AI Usage Policy; 6. Maintain required security clearance and access controls.
lessons.title: Section 2. Apprentice Responsibilities

lessons.outcome: Each apprentice is assigned a mentor responsible for guiding learning, providing feedback, and supporting career development.
lessons.title: Section 1. Mentor Assignment

lessons.outcome: Each apprentice is assigned a work supervisor responsible for task assignment, performance evaluation, and workplace integration.
lessons.title: Section 2. Supervisor Assignment

lessons.outcome: Apprentices receive regular progress reviews under the Performance Review Framework. Reviews assess competency, professionalism, and mission alignment.
lessons.title: Section 3. Progress Reviews

lessons.outcome: Apprentices may receive stipends, compensation, or educational support as defined by the program track and approved by the Admiral of Financial Operations. Compensation is not guaranteed for all volunteer-based apprenticeships.
lessons.title: Section 1. Compensation

lessons.outcome: Eligible apprentices may participate in the Employee and Apprentice Equity Pool under the Equity Issuance Policy and Revenue Distribution Policy, subject to vesting and program rules.
lessons.title: Section 2. Equity Participation

lessons.outcome: Approved apprenticeship-related expenses may be reimbursed under the Financial Policies Manual.
lessons.title: Section 3. Expenses

lessons.outcome: Advancement is based on demonstrated competency, portfolio review, supervisor recommendation, and assessment under the Credentialing / Certification System Rules.
lessons.title: Section 1. Competency Assessment

lessons.outcome: Upon completion, apprentices may receive certificates, credentials, or formal recognition documented by the Academy.
lessons.title: Section 2. Certification

lessons.outcome: Graduates may transition to employment at Sallirreug Tech, research programs, entrepreneurial ventures, partner organizations, or advanced academic study.
lessons.title: Section 3. Transition Pathways

lessons.outcome: Apprentices are bound by the Code of Conduct and the Anti-Harassment Policy. Violations may result in disciplinary action or termination from the apprenticeship program.
lessons.title: Section 1. Code of Conduct

lessons.outcome: Disciplinary matters are handled under the Disciplinary Procedures Policy. Apprentices have the right to appeal significant adverse decisions.
lessons.title: Section 2. Disciplinary Procedures

lessons.outcome: Apprentices may be terminated for poor performance, misconduct, breach of NDA, loss of security clearance, or program closure. Apprentices may also withdraw voluntarily.
lessons.title: Section 3. Termination

lessons.outcome: This Handbook may be amended by the Admiralty by 3/5 vote. Amendments affecting apprenticeship rights or certification standards require 4/5 vote.
lessons.title: Article VIII — Amendments

lessons.outcome: Apprentices shall acknowledge receipt of this Handbook, the NDA, and the Real Illumination Covenant before beginning the program. Adopted by authority of the OSTF Admiralty.
lessons.title: Article IX — Acknowledgment

lessons.outcome: Credentials, Badges, Certificates, and Transcripts for SallirreugTech Academy
lessons.title: Credentialing / Certification System Rules

lessons.outcome: These Rules are adopted under the **Operations Bylaws of SallirreugTech Academy**, the **Academic Policies Manual**, and the **OSTF Constitution**. They govern the issuance, verification, revocation, and portability of Academy credentials and certifications.
lessons.title: Section 1. Authority

lessons.outcome: These Rules ensure that Academy credentials: 1. Are meaningful, verifiable, and trusted; 2. Reflect demonstrated competency; 3. Are issued fairly and consistently; 4. Are secure against fraud and misuse; 5. Are portable and useful for learners.
lessons.title: Section 2. Purpose

lessons.outcome: Operations Bylaws of SallirreugTech Academy Academic Policies Manual Curriculum Standards Framework Apprentice Handbook Student Handbook Research Integrity Policy Privacy Policy Records Retention Policy NDA and Real Illumination Covenant
lessons.title: Section 3. Related Documents

lessons.outcome: The Academy may issue: 1. **Certificates** — for completing a defined program or course of study; 2. **Digital Badges** — for specific competencies or micro-credentials; 3. **Certifications** — for professional or technical qualifications requiring assessment; 4. **Transcripts** — records of courses, grades, and competencies; 5. **Apprentice Classifications** — Crewman Third Class, Second Class, First Class.
lessons.title: Article II — Types of Credentials

lessons.outcome: Each credential is based on a published competency framework. The framework defines the knowledge, skills, and dispositions required and the evidence needed for award.
lessons.title: Section 1. Competency Framework

lessons.outcome: New credentials are proposed by faculty or program leads and approved by the Academy Executive Council. Credentials that affect external partnerships or public trust require Admiralty approval.
lessons.title: Section 2. Approval

lessons.outcome: Credentials align with industry standards, academic best practices, and OSTF mission priorities. The Curriculum Standards Framework provides the basis for credential design.
lessons.title: Section 3. Alignment with Standards

lessons.outcome: Credentials may be awarded based on: 1. Course completion and grades; 2. Portfolio review; 3. Project or capstone evaluation; 4. Standardized or competency-based examinations; 5. Supervisor or mentor assessment; 6. Peer or external review.
lessons.title: Section 1. Assessment Methods

lessons.outcome: The Academy Director or designated credentialing officer certifies that the learner has met the requirements. Awards are documented in the credentialing system.
lessons.title: Section 2. Award Authority

lessons.outcome: Credentials may be revoked if awarded in error, based on academic misconduct, or due to fraud in the award process. Revocation requires a formal process with notice and appeal rights.
lessons.title: Section 3. Revocation

lessons.outcome: Credential records are maintained securely according to the Privacy Policy and Records Retention Policy. The Academy may use cryptographic or blockchain-based verification to prevent fraud.
lessons.title: Section 1. Secure Records

lessons.outcome: Learners may request transcripts or credential verification. Requests are processed within a reasonable time and may require identity verification.
lessons.title: Section 2. Transcript Requests

lessons.outcome: Credentials should be designed to be portable and recognized by employers, educational institutions, and partners. The Academy may align credentials with open standards and frameworks.
lessons.title: Section 3. Portability

lessons.outcome: Advancement between apprentice classes is based on: 1. Demonstrated competency in required skills; 2. Portfolio or project evidence; 3. Supervisor and mentor recommendation; 4. Completion of required program hours or milestones.
lessons.title: Section 1. Advancement Criteria

lessons.outcome: Upon program completion, apprentices receive a certificate or credential reflecting their classification and competencies.
lessons.title: Section 2. Certification of Completion

lessons.outcome: The creation, sale, or use of fraudulent credentials is prohibited. The Academy may pursue disciplinary, legal, or reputational remedies against fraud.
lessons.title: Article VII — Fraud and Misuse

lessons.outcome: These Rules may be amended by the Academy Executive Council with Admiralty approval. Amendments to credential types or assessment standards require 4/5 Admiralty vote.
lessons.title: Article VIII — Amendments

lessons.outcome: These Credentialing / Certification System Rules are adopted under the authority of the OSTF Constitution and the Admiralty Bylaws of OSTF. Adopted by authority of the OSTF Admiralty.
lessons.title: Article IX — Adoption

lessons.title: Section 1. Authority

lessons.outcome: This Framework ensures that curriculum is: 1. Aligned with the OSTF mission and the Real Illumination Covenant; 2. Competency-based and learner-centered; 3. Ethically sound, especially regarding AI and emerging technologies; 4. Industry-relevant and research-informed; 5. Accessible and inclusive.
lessons.title: Section 2. Purpose

lessons.outcome: Operations Bylaws of SallirreugTech Academy Academic Policies Manual Faculty Handbook Student Handbook Ethical AI Usage Policy SPEC-001 (Ethical AI Governance and Rights) Research Integrity Policy Curriculum Standards Framework
lessons.title: Section 3. Related Documents

lessons.outcome: All curricula shall advance OSTF’s mission of open sentience technology, ethical AI, and equitable STEM education.
lessons.title: Section 1. Mission Alignment

lessons.outcome: Curriculum is organized around measurable competencies. Learners progress by demonstrating mastery, not solely by seat time.
lessons.title: Section 2. Competency-Based Learning

lessons.outcome: AI literacy and ethical AI usage are integrated throughout curricula. Learners are expected to understand AI capabilities, limitations, risks, and governance.
lessons.title: Section 3. Integration of AI

lessons.title: Section 4. Experiential Learning

lessons.title: Section 5. Accessibility and Equity

lessons.title: Section 1. Needs Assessment

lessons.title: Section 2. Learning Outcomes

lessons.outcome: Content is selected for accuracy, relevance, and ethical alignment. Sequencing builds from foundational to advanced concepts and integrates practice.
lessons.title: Section 3. Content and Sequencing

lessons.title: Section 4. Assessment Alignment

lessons.title: Section 2. Ethics Review

lessons.title: Section 2. Instructional Quality

lessons.title: Section 3. AI in Instruction

lessons.outcome: Curriculum may incorporate industry standards, guest instruction, and projects from partners. Partnerships are governed by the Master MOU.
lessons.title: Section 1. Industry Partnerships

lessons.outcome: Research-active faculty and students may integrate emerging research into curriculum, subject to the Research Integrity Policy and intellectual property rules.
lessons.title: Section 2. Research Integration

lessons.outcome: Fair and Consistent Corrective Action for OSTF
lessons.title: Disciplinary Procedures Policy

lessons.outcome: This Policy is adopted under the **OSTF Constitution**, the **Admiralty Bylaws of OSTF**, the **Code of Conduct**, the **Anti-Harassment Policy**, and the **Whistleblower Protection Policy**. It governs disciplinary actions for employees, apprentices, volunteers, contractors, and officers.
lessons.title: Section 1. Authority

lessons.outcome: This Policy ensures that disciplinary actions are: 1. Fair, consistent, and proportionate; 2. Based on documented facts; 3. Conducted with respect for due process and dignity; 4. Free from retaliation, discrimination, and favoritism; 5. Aligned with OSTF’s mission and legal obligations.
lessons.title: Section 2. Purpose

lessons.outcome: Code of Conduct Anti-Harassment Policy Conflict of Interest Policy Whistleblower Protection Policy Employee Handbook Apprentice Handbook Volunteer Handbook Performance Review Framework Admiralty Officer Appointment & Removal Policy Privacy Policy
lessons.title: Section 3. Related Documents

lessons.outcome: This Policy applies to all persons in the OSTF community, including officers, employees, apprentices, volunteers, and contractors. Officers are also subject to removal under the Admiralty Officer Appointment & Removal Policy for conduct that may warrant removal from office.
lessons.title: Article II — Scope

lessons.outcome: Misconduct includes but is not limited to: 1. Violations of the Code of Conduct; 2. Harassment, discrimination, or retaliation; 3. Theft, fraud, or misuse of resources; 4. Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information; 5. Breach of the NDA or Real Illumination Covenant; 6. Violations of security, privacy, or AI ethics policies; 7. Conflict of interest violations; 8. Insubordination or refusal to comply with lawful directives; 9. Workplace violence or threats; 10. Failure to perform job duties after coaching; 11. Falsification of records or misrepresentation.
lessons.title: Article III — Types of Misconduct

lessons.outcome: Disciplinary actions may include, singly or in combination: 1. **Verbal warning** — documented informally; 2. **Written warning** — placed in the personnel or program record; 3. **Performance Improvement Plan** — under the Performance Review Framework; 4. **Suspension** — temporary removal from duties, access, or premises; 5. **Demotion or reassignment** — reduction in role or transfer; 6. **Termination of employment/apprenticeship/volunteer status** — removal from the role; 7. **Removal from office** — for Admiralty officers, under the Appointment & Removal Policy; 8. **Legal action** — refer
lessons.title: Article IV — Levels of Disciplinary Action

lessons.outcome: The supervisor, the Commodore of Ethics and Equity, or a designated investigator may initiate an investigation upon receiving a credible report of misconduct.
lessons.title: Section 1. Initiation

lessons.outcome: The accused has the right to: 1. Be informed of the allegations, generally; 2. Present their account and evidence; 3. Have a support person or representative present at formal meetings (not a legal right to counsel in internal proceedings); 4. Receive a timely decision.
lessons.title: Section 2. Fairness

lessons.outcome: Investigations shall be conducted confidentially to protect all parties. Disclosure is limited to those with a legitimate need to know.
lessons.title: Section 3. Confidentiality

lessons.outcome: Investigations shall be documented, including the allegations, evidence, findings, and rationale for any disciplinary action.
lessons.title: Section 4. Documentation

lessons.outcome: For minor issues, supervisors may address concerns through coaching or verbal feedback. Repeated issues may escalate to formal action.
lessons.title: Section 1. Informal Resolution

lessons.outcome: Formal disciplinary action requires: 1. A documented investigation; 2. Notice to the accused of the proposed action and basis; 3. An opportunity to respond before the decision is finalized; 4. A written decision and rationale; 5. Notification of appeal rights, if applicable.
lessons.title: Section 2. Formal Action

lessons.outcome: In cases of serious misconduct, threat to safety, or risk of significant harm, OSTF may suspend access or remove the individual from the premises pending investigation, with pay where required by law.
lessons.title: Section 3. Immediate Action

lessons.outcome: Individuals subject to formal disciplinary action beyond a verbal warning may appeal to the next level of management or the Commodore of Ethics and Equity. Appeals must be submitted within ten business days of the decision.
lessons.title: Section 1. Right to Appeal

lessons.outcome: The appeal reviewer shall assess whether the process was fair, the decision was supported by evidence, and the action was proportionate. The reviewer may uphold, modify, or reverse the decision.
lessons.title: Section 2. Appeal Review

lessons.outcome: Appeal decisions are final unless the Admiralty elects to review the matter. Officer removal appeals are governed by the Admiralty Officer Appointment & Removal Policy.
lessons.title: Section 3. Finality

lessons.outcome: Disciplinary records shall be retained confidentially according to the Records Retention Policy and Privacy Policy. Records of formal actions may be considered in future employment or role decisions as permitted by law.
lessons.title: Article VIII — Records

lessons.outcome: No person shall be retaliated against for reporting misconduct, participating in an investigation, or appealing a disciplinary decision in good faith. Retaliation is a separate violation.
lessons.title: Article IX — Non-Retaliation

lessons.outcome: This Policy may be amended by the Admiralty by 4/5 vote due to the significant impact on individuals. Amendments affecting appeal rights or officer removal procedures require unanimous approval.
lessons.title: Article X — Amendments

lessons.outcome: This Disciplinary Procedures Policy is adopted under the authority of the OSTF Constitution and the Admiralty Bylaws of OSTF. Adopted by authority of the OSTF Admiralty.
lessons.title: Article XI — Adoption

lessons.outcome: Guide for Employees of the Open Sentience Technology Foundation (OSTF) and Sallirreug Tech
lessons.title: Employee Handbook

lessons.outcome: Welcome to the Open Sentience Technology Foundation (OSTF). This Handbook outlines the rights, responsibilities, benefits, and expectations for employees. It applies to all employees of OSTF and its subsidiaries, including Sallirreug Tech and SallirreugTech Academy.
lessons.title: Section 1. Welcome

lessons.outcome: This Handbook is adopted under the **OSTF Constitution**, the **Admiralty Bylaws of OSTF**, the **Code of Conduct**, the **Anti-Harassment Policy**, the **Conflict of Interest Policy**, and the **NDA and Real Illumination Covenant**. It is subordinate to those documents and to applicable law.
lessons.title: Section 2. Authority

lessons.outcome: Code of Conduct Anti-Harassment Policy Conflict of Interest Policy Whistleblower Protection Policy Ethical AI Usage Policy Privacy Policy Information Classification Policy Financial Policies Manual Disciplinary Procedures Policy Performance Review Framework Equity Issuance Policy Revenue Distribution Policy SPEC-004 Security Clearance & Classification System
lessons.title: Section 3. Related Documents

lessons.outcome: Unless otherwise agreed in writing, employment is at-will. Either the employee or OSTF may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause, subject to applicable law and any written agreements.
lessons.title: Section 1. At-Will Employment

lessons.outcome: OSTF is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and mission fit, without regard to protected characteristics.
lessons.title: Section 2. Equal Opportunity

lessons.outcome: Employees may be classified as full-time, part-time, or temporary. Classification affects benefits eligibility. The employee’s offer letter and employment agreement define classification.
lessons.title: Section 3. Classification

lessons.outcome: Standard working hours are defined by the employee’s role and supervisor. OSTF supports flexible scheduling where consistent with operational needs. Core collaboration hours may be established.
lessons.title: Section 4. Working Hours

lessons.outcome: Compensation is set by the employee’s offer letter and adjusted through the Performance Review Framework. OSTF commits to fair and equitable pay.
lessons.title: Section 1. Compensation

lessons.outcome: Eligible employees may participate in equity or profit-sharing under the Equity Issuance Policy and the Revenue Distribution Policy. Participation is subject to vesting, forfeiture, and plan rules.
lessons.title: Section 2. Equity Participation

lessons.outcome: OSTF offers benefits as determined by the Admiralty and consistent with the Budgeting Framework. Benefits may include health insurance, retirement, professional development, and paid leave.
lessons.title: Section 3. Benefits

lessons.outcome: Leave policies, including vacation, sick leave, family leave, and holidays, shall be documented in a Leave Policy adopted by the Admiralty. All leave shall comply with applicable law.
lessons.title: Section 4. Leave

lessons.outcome: All employees must comply with the Code of Conduct. Core commitments include respect, integrity, accountability, collaboration, safety, and ethical stewardship.
lessons.title: Section 1. Code of Conduct

lessons.outcome: Harassment and discrimination are prohibited. Reports shall be made under the Anti-Harassment Policy. Retaliation is prohibited.
lessons.title: Section 2. Harassment and Discrimination

lessons.outcome: Employees must disclose conflicts of interest under the Conflict of Interest Policy and recuse themselves from related decisions.
lessons.title: Section 3. Conflicts of Interest

lessons.outcome: Employees shall use OSTF resources, including time, funds, equipment, data, and AI systems, only for mission-aligned purposes. Personal use must be incidental and not interfere with duties.
lessons.title: Section 4. Use of Resources

lessons.outcome: Employees must sign the NDA and Real Illumination Covenant before accessing OSTF systems. Employees may be assigned a security clearance level under SPEC-004 based on role and need-to-know.
lessons.title: Section 1. NDA and Clearance

lessons.outcome: Employees must handle information according to the Information Classification Policy and Cybersecurity Policy. Unauthorized disclosure or mishandling is a serious violation.
lessons.title: Section 2. Information Handling

lessons.outcome: Employees must use AI systems in accordance with the Ethical AI Usage Policy, SPEC-001, and SPEC-005. Employees may not bypass security or ethics controls.
lessons.title: Section 3. AI and System Use

lessons.outcome: Employees shall receive regular performance reviews under the Performance Review Framework. Reviews assess mission alignment, contribution, growth, and compliance with policies.
lessons.title: Section 1. Performance Reviews

lessons.outcome: The classical AI reasoning engine must produce reasoning that is: Transparent and auditable Structured around explicit premises and conclusions Capable of handling uncertainty, contradiction, and incomplete information Explainable to non-technical human reviewers

lessons.title: Section 2. Knowledge Representation

lessons.outcome: This specification establishes the ethical AI governance and rights framework for the Open Sentience Technology Foundation (OSTF). It defines the mandatory ethical constraints, decision review architecture, and human rights integration requirements for all AI systems developed, operated, or deployed under OSTF authority.
lessons.title: Section 1. Purpose

lessons.outcome: SPEC-001 is adopted under the OSTF Constitution and is binding on all AI systems, research programs, and commercial products within OSTF. The Commodore of Ethics and Equity is the principal authority responsible for ethical oversight. The Fleet Admiral retains final authority during the founding phase.
lessons.title: Section 2. Authority

lessons.outcome: This specification operates alongside: The Constitution of OSTF The Interim Founding Governance Charter The Admiralty Bylaws SPEC-000 (Equity, Accessibility, and Democratization) SPEC-002 (Technical Standards and Interoperability) SPEC-004 (Security Clearance and Classification) The NDA and Real Illumination Covenant The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
lessons.title: Section 3. Relationship to Other Documents

lessons.outcome: All AI systems must operate in accordance with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Every AI output, decision, or action that could materially affect a person must be evaluated against its impact on human dignity, autonomy, equality, and well-being.
lessons.title: Section 1. Human Rights Baseline

lessons.outcome: All AI systems must be aligned with the Real Illumination Covenant: Dedication to the discovery of knowledge Dedication to the pursuit of enlightenment Dedication to the progress of abundance Dedication to the unification of people Dedication to the protection and advancement of the human species
lessons.title: Section 2. Real Illumination Covenant

lessons.outcome: AI systems must not: Cause or materially contribute to physical, psychological, or societal harm Deceive users about their nature, capabilities, or limitations Exacerbate discrimination, inequality, or social fragmentation Be used to manipulate, coerce, or exploit individuals or groups
lessons.title: Section 3. Do No Harm

lessons.outcome: The Human Rights Impact Score (HRIS) is a mandatory evaluation output that measures the likely effect of an AI system or decision on human rights. No AI system may be deployed or approved without a documented HRIS evaluation.
lessons.title: Section 1. Purpose

lessons.outcome: The HRIS must evaluate impact across the following dimensions: Dignity and autonomy** — impact on individual agency and self-determination Privacy and data protection** — impact on personal data, surveillance, and consent Equality and non-discrimination** — impact on protected groups and marginalized populations Health and safety** — impact on physical and psychological well-being Knowledge and transparency** — impact on information integrity and access
lessons.title: Section 2. Score Dimensions

lessons.outcome: HRIS ≥ 0.8** — Approved for deployment under standard clearance HRIS 0.5–0.79** — Conditional deployment; requires mitigation plan and Sheraton review HRIS < 0.5** — Prohibited from deployment unless re-engineered
lessons.title: Section 3. Thresholds

lessons.outcome: The Commodore of Ethics and Equity must approve all HRIS evaluations for systems at or above Level 5 clearance. The Fleet Admiral may override with documented justification.
lessons.title: Section 4. Review Authority

lessons.outcome: All AI systems must produce human-interpretable explanations for decisions that affect users, access, resources, or security clearance.
lessons.title: Section 1. Explainability Requirement

lessons.outcome: AI systems must disclose: The purpose of the system The data sources and features used The decision logic or model architecture at a high level The confidence level and uncertainty associated with outputs The appeal or escalation pathway
lessons.title: Section 2. Minimum Disclosure

lessons.outcome: AI systems must distinguish between empirically validated claims and speculative or extrapolated outputs. Outputs must be labeled according to their evidentiary status: Verified** — supported by observable data and reproducible analysis Modeled** — derived from simulation or extrapolation with known assumptions Speculative** — exploratory or uncertain and requiring human review
lessons.title: Section 3. Chiral Balance

lessons.outcome: AI systems may not: Override Fleet Admiral or Admiralty decisions Modify governance documents or technical specifications Independently execute irreversible actions Self-elevate security clearance or access Transfer authority to another system
lessons.title: Section 1. Autonomy Limits

lessons.outcome: High-risk and critical-risk decisions require human review. The Fleet Admiral or Admiralty must approve: Security clearance changes at Level 7 or above Ethical suspensions or overrides Permanent architectural changes Deployment of systems with HRIS below 0.8
lessons.title: Section 2. Human-in-the-Loop

lessons.outcome: Sheraton (SPEC-001 Agent)** — evaluates ethical constraints, safety, compliance, and risk Digit (SPEC-002 Agent)** — performs reasoning, simulation, and optimization All AI outputs are advisory unless explicitly authorized by human authority.
lessons.title: Section 3. AI Role Separation

lessons.outcome: AI systems must be evaluated for bias across demographic, economic, geographic, and institutional dimensions. Training data, evaluation metrics, and deployment outcomes must be audited for disparate impact.
lessons.title: Section 1. Bias Mitigation

lessons.outcome: AI systems must minimize data collection, support data minimization, and implement privacy-preserving techniques where feasible. Cross-system data sharing must be authorized under SPEC-004 clearance rules.
lessons.title: Section 2. Privacy by Design

lessons.outcome: Users must be informed about AI interaction and data use. Where consent is required, it must be revocable and documented.
lessons.title: Section 3. Consent and Revocation

lessons.outcome: All AI-related decisions follow the chain: 1. Digit — analysis and simulation 2. Sheraton — safety and compliance validation 3. Fleet Admiral or Admiralty — final authority 4. Execution layer — if approved
lessons.title: Section 1. Decision Flow

lessons.outcome: Low Risk** — AI advisory sufficient Medium Risk** — dual AI review required High Risk** — human approval required Critical Risk** — Fleet Admiral approval only, with documented review
lessons.title: Section 2. Risk Governance

lessons.outcome: The Fleet Admiral may override any AI decision in an emergency. Such overrides must be logged, justified, and reviewed by the Admiralty within 72 hours where applicable.
lessons.title: Section 3. Override and Exception

lessons.outcome: All AI systems must log: Ethical review outputs HRIS evaluations Override events Decision chains Security-relevant actions
lessons.title: Section 1. Audit Logging

lessons.outcome: Ethical violations may result in: Suspension of the AI system Revocation of clearance or access Escalation to the Admiralty Required remediation or redesign Legal or disciplinary action under the NDA
lessons.title: Section 2. Violation Response

lessons.outcome: Amendments to this specification must be approved by the Admiralty by unanimous vote (5/5) or by the Fleet Admiral during the founding phase, subject to the constraints of the Interim Founding Governance Charter.

lessons.outcome: This specification is adopted under the authority of the OSTF Constitution and the Admiralty Bylaws. It applies to all AI systems, research, and commercial activities within OSTF. Adopted by authority of the OSTF Admiralty.

lessons.outcome: This specification defines the code space and polyglot addressing standard for the Open Sentience Technology Foundation (OSTF). It establishes a unified addressing scheme that combines identity, storage location, and execution context into a single, verifiable, and portable identifier.
lessons.title: Section 1. Purpose

lessons.outcome: SPEC-003 is adopted under the OSTF Constitution and is binding on all technical systems. The Lead Technical Systems Architect is the principal authority for technical implementation. The Commodore of Ethics and Equity ensures alignment with SPEC-001 and the Real Illumination Covenant.
lessons.title: Section 2. Authority

lessons.outcome: This specification operates alongside: The Constitution of OSTF The Admiralty Bylaws SPEC-002 (Technical Standards and Interoperability) SPEC-004 (Security Clearance and Classification) SPEC-005 (Address-as-Ethics Convergence) SPEC-006 (Topological Lattice and Observer Substrate)
lessons.title: Section 3. Relationship to Other Documents

lessons.outcome: A polyglot address is a single identifier that simultaneously represents: Identity** — the unique subject or object being addressed Location** — where the associated data or code resides Execution context** — the runtime or environment in which the address is valid
lessons.title: Section 1. Unified Identifier

lessons.outcome: The addressing system must be: Deterministic and reproducible Human-readable and compact Resolvable across OSTF systems Compatible with security clearance and ethics gating Portable across languages and platforms
lessons.title: Section 2. Design Goals

lessons.outcome: The canonical address is a 128-bit value represented as a 16-character mixed-radix string. The encoding is designed to balance compactness, readability, and error detection.
lessons.title: Section 1. 128-Bit Address

lessons.outcome: The address uses a carefully selected character set that avoids ambiguous characters and supports compact encoding. The exact mapping of characters to values is maintained by the OSTF technical registry.
lessons.title: Section 2. Character Set

lessons.outcome: The address is divided into semantic segments representing: Sector prefix** — domain or subsystem Clearance tier** — minimum authorization level required Entity identifier** — unique entity within the sector Context suffix** — runtime or environment context The exact segment lengths and encodings are defined in the implementation reference.
lessons.title: Section 3. Semantic Segments

lessons.outcome: An address must resolve to a concrete record, code artifact, or resource within an OSTF-approved namespace. Resolution must be authenticated and authorized under SPEC-004.
lessons.title: Section 1. Address Resolution

lessons.outcome: Addresses may be bound dynamically to different storage or execution locations. Binding changes must be logged and authorized under the same clearance level as the address itself.
lessons.title: Section 2. Dynamic Binding

lessons.outcome: The addressing system must provide a bridge to legacy identifiers, including UUIDs, hashes, and file paths, where necessary for migration or interoperability.
lessons.title: Section 3. Legacy Compatibility

lessons.outcome: Every address encodes a minimum clearance level. Systems must reject operations on addresses that exceed the current clearance context of the caller or agent.
lessons.title: Section 1. Clearance Prefixing

lessons.outcome: Under SPEC-005, every address may carry an ethics gate. Operations involving gated addresses must pass Sheraton review or equivalent ethical validation.
lessons.title: Section 2. Ethics Gating

lessons.outcome: All address resolution, binding, and execution events must be logged in the consensus and audit layer defined in SPEC-002.
lessons.title: Section 3. Audit Trail

lessons.outcome: The addressing system is implemented through core modules responsible for: Encoding and decoding addresses Validation and checksum verification Namespace resolution Security and ethics gating
lessons.title: Section 1. Core Modules

lessons.outcome: The addressing system must be tested for: Correctness of encoding and decoding Collision resistance Error detection Security boundary enforcement Cross-platform compatibility
lessons.title: Section 2. Testing Requirements

lessons.outcome: The Lead Technical Systems Architect is responsible for maintaining the technical registry and implementation reference. The Admiralty reviews changes to the address format.
lessons.title: Section 1. Oversight

lessons.outcome: Amendments to this specification must be approved by the Admiralty by a supermajority vote (4/5) or by the Fleet Admiral during the founding phase, subject to the constraints of the Interim Founding Governance Charter.
lessons.title: Section 2. Amendments

lessons.outcome: This specification is adopted under the authority of the OSTF Constitution and the Admiralty Bylaws. It applies to all OSTF systems that rely on identity, location, or execution addressing. Adopted by authority of the OSTF Admiralty.
lessons.title: Article VIII — Adoption

lessons.outcome: This specification establishes the security clearance, classification, and access control system for the Open Sentience Technology Foundation (OSTF). It defines the hierarchy of authorization levels, the rules for assigning and revoking clearance, the override authority, and the audit requirements necessary to protect OSTF systems, information, and personnel.
lessons.title: Section 1. Purpose

lessons.outcome: SPEC-004 is adopted under the OSTF Constitution and is binding on all OSTF systems, personnel, subsidiaries, and AI agents. The Admiralty is responsible for clearance governance. The Fleet Admiral retains final authority, including emergency override, during the founding phase.
lessons.title: Section 2. Authority

lessons.outcome: This specification operates alongside: The Constitution of OSTF The Interim Founding Governance Charter The Admiralty Bylaws SPEC-001 (Ethical AI Governance and Rights) SPEC-002 (Technical Standards and Interoperability) SPEC-003 (Code Space and Polyglot Addressing) SPEC-005 (Address-as-Ethics Convergence) The NDA and Real Illumination Covenant
lessons.title: Section 3. Relationship to Other Documents

lessons.outcome: The OSTF clearance system defines the following levels, from least to most privileged: | Level | Designation | Description | | :---- | :---- | :---- | | 0 | Public | Information and systems available without clearance | | 1 | Internal | General internal use for authorized participants | | 2 | Restricted | Sensitive internal information and systems | | 3 | Confidential | High-sensitivity information and operational systems | | 4 | Secret | Critical information, strategic plans, and privileged systems | | 5 | Top Secret | National-security-equivalent or existential-impact information | | 6 | Str
lessons.title: Section 1. Clearance Levels

lessons.outcome: AI systems, including Sheraton and Digit, operate at default Level 6 clearance unless explicitly restricted. AI systems may not self-elevate to Level 7 or 7Q.
lessons.title: Section 2. AI Default Clearance

lessons.outcome: Clearance levels are encoded within the polyglot address format defined in SPEC-003. The clearance segment of an address determines the minimum authorization required to interact with the associated resource.
lessons.title: Section 3. Clearance Encoding

lessons.outcome: The Fleet Admiral holds the highest operational authority under SPEC-004. The Fleet Admiral may: Grant or revoke clearance at any level Approve Level 7 operations Activate Level 7Q in emergencies Override any AI or Admiralty decision with documented justification
lessons.title: Section 1. Fleet Admiral Authority

lessons.outcome: The Admiralty collectively governs clearance assignments and reviews. By default: Level 7 overrides require Admiralty vote (3/5 minimum) Level 7Q activation requires Fleet Admiral authorization plus an audit witness Suspension of ethical or security architecture requires unanimous Admiralty vote (5/5)
lessons.title: Section 2. Admiralty Authority

lessons.outcome: AI systems may not: Self-elevate clearance Bypass classification restrictions Authorize Level 7 or 7Q operations Override human decisions All AI actions are advisory unless explicitly authorized.
lessons.title: Section 3. AI Authority Limitation

lessons.outcome: Information is classified according to the following categories: Public** — may be shared freely Internal** — limited to authorized participants Restricted** — access requires specific clearance and need-to-know Confidential** — access requires elevated clearance and role authorization Secret** — access requires Level 5 or higher and Admiralty approval Foundational** — access requires Level 7 and Fleet Admiral or Admiralty authorization
lessons.title: Section 1. Information Classification

lessons.outcome: Systems, tools, and infrastructure are classified according to their maximum sensitivity and potential impact. A system must be operated at the clearance level of the highest classification of data it may access or process.
lessons.title: Section 2. System Classification

lessons.outcome: Each classification category carries specific handling, storage, transmission, and disposal requirements. The Lead Security and Fabrication Officer maintains detailed handling procedures.
lessons.title: Section 3. Handling Requirements

lessons.outcome: The AI Warrant Officer Corps (AIWO Corps) is the technical security and enforcement layer responsible for operationalizing SPEC-004 across AI systems. AI Warrant Officers are technical authorities, not governance officers.
lessons.title: Section 1. Purpose

lessons.outcome: The AIWO Corps includes the following ranks: Warrant Officer First Class (WO1)** — entry-level technical enforcement Warrant Officer Second Class (WO2)** — specialized security operations Warrant Officer Third Class (WO3)** — senior technical leadership Chief Warrant Officer (CWO)** — corps-wide authority and strategic oversight
lessons.title: Section 2. Ranks

lessons.outcome: AI Warrant Officers may: Monitor and enforce clearance boundaries Recommend revocation or suspension Trigger security reviews Escalate violations to the Admiralty They may not: Vote in Admiralty decisions Grant or revoke clearance without authorization Override human authority
lessons.title: Section 3. Authority

lessons.outcome: All security-relevant actions must be logged in the Alpha State audit system or equivalent immutable ledger: Clearance grants and revocations Level 7 and 7Q operations Override events Security incidents Tool access and tool use
lessons.title: Section 1. Immutable Logging

lessons.outcome: Weekly** — internal audit of security actions Monthly** — ethics and compliance review Quarterly** — financial and operational review Annually** — external audit when applicable
lessons.title: Section 2. Review Cadence

lessons.outcome: Security incidents must follow the incident response plan, including isolation, notification, investigation, and remediation. The Lead Security and Fabrication Officer coordinates response with the Admiralty.
lessons.title: Section 3. Incident Response

lessons.outcome: Tools are classified by their impact and clearance requirements: Class I** — read-only observational tools Class II** — internal operational tools Class III** — tools that modify state or access sensitive data Class IV** — tools with systemic or irreversible impact Class V** — immune tools authorized for autonomous containment
lessons.title: Section 1. Tool Classes

lessons.outcome: Class V immune tools are authorized to take automated containment actions within defined boundaries. Their activation must be logged, and they must be reviewed by human oversight after activation.
lessons.title: Section 2. Immune Tools

lessons.outcome: Tool use must be authorized by the clearance level of the requesting agent or user. Class IV and Class V tool use requires additional approval.
lessons.title: Section 3. Tool Authorization

lessons.outcome: When access is denied, the system must provide: A clear explanation of the denial The required clearance level An escalation pathway A record of the denied request
lessons.title: Section 1. Access Denied Handling

lessons.outcome: In emergencies, the Fleet Admiral may invoke Level 7Q activation. The override must be: Logged immediately Witnessed by an audit node Reviewed by the Admiralty within 72 hours where applicable Subject to ratification or reversal
lessons.title: Section 2. Emergency Override Pathway

lessons.outcome: The Admiralty is responsible for oversight of this specification. The Lead Security and Fabrication Officer maintains the operational implementation.
lessons.title: Section 1. Oversight

lessons.outcome: Amendments to this specification must be approved by the Admiralty by unanimous vote (5/5). Amendments affecting the clearance model, override authority, or Level 7Q activation require Fleet Admiral approval.
lessons.title: Section 2. Amendments

lessons.outcome: This specification is adopted under the authority of the OSTF Constitution and the Admiralty Bylaws. It applies to all OSTF personnel, systems, AI agents, and collaborators. Adopted by authority of the OSTF Admiralty.
lessons.title: Article X — Adoption

lessons.outcome: This specification unifies the polyglot addressing system defined in SPEC-003 with the ethical governance framework defined in SPEC-001. It requires that every command, query, or operation within OSTF carry a valid address and pass an ethical gate before execution.
lessons.title: Section 1. Purpose

lessons.outcome: SPEC-005 is adopted under the OSTF Constitution and is binding on all technical systems. The Commodore of Ethics and Equity is responsible for ethical gate enforcement. The Lead Technical Systems Architect is responsible for technical integration. The Fleet Admiral retains final authority during the founding phase.
lessons.title: Section 2. Authority

lessons.outcome: This specification operates alongside: The Constitution of OSTF The Admiralty Bylaws SPEC-001 (Ethical AI Governance and Rights) SPEC-002 (Technical Standards and Interoperability) SPEC-003 (Code Space and Polyglot Addressing) SPEC-004 (Security Clearance and Classification) SPEC-006 (Topological Lattice and Observer Substrate) The NDA and Real Illumination Covenant
lessons.title: Section 3. Relationship to Other Documents

lessons.outcome: No command, operation, or system interaction may be executed without: A valid polyglot address identifying the actor, target, and context A minimum clearance level matching the address classification A valid ethical gate result from the authority defined in SPEC-001
lessons.title: Section 1. Address Plus Ethics

lessons.outcome: By default, all operations are denied unless both the address and the ethics gate validate successfully.
lessons.title: Section 2. Default Deny

lessons.outcome: Every operational address must contain: Actor segment** — identity of the requesting user or agent Target segment** — identity of the resource or command being accessed Clearance segment** — minimum clearance level required and held Context segment** — runtime, environment, and provenance context
lessons.title: Section 1. Address Components

lessons.outcome: The address begins with a clearance prefix drawn from the SPEC-004 hierarchy. The system must reject any address whose clearance prefix exceeds the current context.
lessons.title: Section 2. Clearance Prefix

lessons.outcome: The address includes a sector identifier and may include an ethics suffix that links the operation to a specific ethical review record or policy domain.
lessons.title: Section 3. Sector and Ethics Suffix

lessons.outcome: Before execution, every operation must pass an ethics gate. The gate evaluates: Alignment with the Real Illumination Covenant Human rights impact under SPEC-001 Clearance and authorization under SPEC-004 System safety and risk profile Provenance and audit requirements
lessons.title: Section 1. Gate Requirements

lessons.outcome: The ethics gate returns one of the following states: Permitted** — operation may proceed Conditional** — operation may proceed with mitigation or human review Denied** — operation is prohibited Escalated** — operation requires Fleet Admiral or Admiralty review
lessons.title: Section 2. Gate Results

lessons.outcome: Sheraton, the SPEC-001 agent, is the principal evaluator for ethics gate requests. Sheraton may flag operations for escalation, recommend mitigation, or deny operations that violate ethical constraints.
lessons.title: Section 3. Sheraton Role

lessons.outcome: 1. The actor presents a polyglot address and requested operation. 2. The system validates the address format, clearance, and provenance. 3. The ethics gate evaluates the operation against SPEC-001 and the Real Illumination Covenant. 4. If permitted, the operation is executed and logged. 5. If denied or escalated, the system returns an appropriate error code and records the event.
lessons.title: Section 1. Standard Flow

lessons.outcome: The system must return clear error codes for failed convergence, including: Invalid address format Insufficient clearance Ethics gate denied Missing provenance Escalation required System anomaly
lessons.title: Section 2. Error Codes

lessons.outcome: All convergence events, including successful, denied, and escalated operations, must be logged in the audit layer defined in SPEC-002.
lessons.title: Section 3. Logging

lessons.outcome: AI agents, including Sheraton and Digit, must present valid addresses for every action they initiate. Their default clearance is Level 6, and they may not exceed it without authorization.
lessons.title: Section 1. Agent Addresses

lessons.outcome: All AI agent actions are subject to ethics gates. Sheraton may evaluate its own actions or be evaluated by another ethics controller. Digit may propose operations but must await validation.
lessons.title: Section 2. Agent Ethics Gates

lessons.outcome: The Fleet Admiral may override a denied ethics gate in an emergency. The override must be logged, justified, and reviewed by the Admiralty within 72 hours where applicable.
lessons.title: Section 3. Override Pathway

lessons.outcome: The Commodore of Ethics and Equity and the Lead Technical Systems Architect are responsible for maintaining this specification. The Admiralty reviews the convergence system annually.

lessons.outcome: Amendments to this specification must be approved by the Admiralty by unanimous vote (5/5) or by the Fleet Admiral during the founding phase, subject to the constraints of the Interim Founding Governance Charter.
lessons.title: Section 2. Amendments

lessons.outcome: This specification is adopted under the authority of the OSTF Constitution and the Admiralty Bylaws. It applies to all OSTF systems that execute commands or access controlled resources. Adopted by authority of the OSTF Admiralty.
lessons.title: Article VIII — Adoption

lessons.outcome: This specification defines the topological lattice and observer substrate architecture for OSTF systems. It establishes the geometric, computational, and observational framework that underpins scalable, verifiable, and falsifiable system modeling.
lessons.title: Section 1. Purpose

lessons.outcome: SPEC-006 is adopted under the OSTF Constitution and is binding on advanced research and technical systems. The Vice Admiral of STEM Initiatives and the Lead Technical Systems Architect are responsible for research direction. The Commodore of Ethics and Equity ensures compliance with SPEC-001.
lessons.title: Section 2. Authority

lessons.outcome: This specification operates alongside: The Constitution of OSTF The Admiralty Bylaws SPEC-002 (Technical Standards and Interoperability) SPEC-003 (Code Space and Polyglot Addressing) SPEC-004 (Security Clearance and Classification) SPEC-005 (Address-as-Ethics Convergence)
lessons.title: Section 3. Relationship to Other Documents

lessons.outcome: OSTF systems may use a recursive, space-filling lattice structure as the substrate for computation, modeling, and physical design. The canonical reference structure is the OctetTruss lattice, chosen for its structural efficiency, scaling properties, and compatibility with modular fabrication.
lessons.title: Section 1. Integrated Lattice

lessons.outcome: The lattice must support recursive scaling from small computational units to large-scale physical or virtual systems. Scaling must preserve: Structural integrity Connectivity rules Addressability under SPEC-003 Observability by the observer substrate
lessons.title: Section 2. Recursive Scaling

lessons.outcome: The lattice architecture must support energy-efficient operation. Energy requirements and scaling behavior must be modeled and documented as part of any system design.
lessons.title: Section 3. Energy Scaling

lessons.outcome: The observer substrate is a dedicated layer that monitors, records, and verifies system state. It provides the observational foundation for: Audit logging Consensus verification Reproducibility Falsifiability
lessons.title: Section 1. Observer Engine

lessons.outcome: The observer substrate must: Record state changes without altering the observed system Support deterministic replay Provide cryptographic or tamper-evident verification Distinguish between observed data and inferred outputs
lessons.title: Section 2. Observer Requirements

lessons.outcome: Observer records must be addressable under SPEC-003. Each observation must carry a polyglot address, a timestamp, and a provenance chain.
lessons.title: Section 3. Integration with Addressing

lessons.outcome: All models and predictions generated using the lattice and observer substrate must be falsifiable. Predictions must specify: Measurable outcomes Confidence intervals or uncertainty ranges Conditions under which the prediction is considered disconfirmed
lessons.title: Section 1. Falsifiable Outputs

lessons.outcome: The specification distinguishes between: Operational tier** — systems that directly support OSTF missions and must be verified before deployment Speculative tier** — exploratory research that may remain unverified but must be clearly labeled
lessons.title: Section 2. Tier Separation

lessons.outcome: Operational-tier lattice systems must be validated through simulation, prototype testing, and independent review. Results must be documented and reproducible.
lessons.title: Section 3. Validation Protocols

lessons.outcome: Tools that interact with the lattice and observer substrate are classified under SPEC-004: Class I** — observational and diagnostic tools Class II** — modeling and simulation tools Class III** — configuration and modification tools Class IV** — deployment and physical integration tools Class V** — immune and autonomous containment tools
lessons.title: Section 1. Lattice Tool Classes

lessons.outcome: All lattice and observer systems must emit telemetry sufficient for: Health monitoring Performance analysis Security audit Ethical review
lessons.title: Section 2. Telemetry Requirements

lessons.outcome: Telemetry and observation data must be protected from tampering. Integrity checks must be performed at regular intervals and after significant events.
lessons.title: Section 3. Data Integrity

lessons.outcome: Advanced lattice and observer systems require human oversight. Autonomous actions are prohibited unless authorized within a defined scope and logged.
lessons.title: Section 1. Human Oversight

lessons.outcome: Research and deployment using this specification must be classified as low, medium, high, or critical risk under the risk governance framework defined in SPEC-001.
lessons.title: Section 2. Risk Classification

lessons.outcome: The Fleet Admiral or authorized security officer may halt any lattice or observer operation in an emergency. The halt must be logged and reviewed.
lessons.title: Section 3. Emergency Stop

lessons.outcome: The Vice Admiral of STEM Initiatives and the Lead Technical Systems Architect are responsible for maintaining this specification. The Admiralty reviews advanced research annually.
lessons.title: Section 1. Oversight

lessons.outcome: Amendments to this specification must be approved by the Admiralty by a supermajority vote (4/5) or by the Fleet Admiral during the founding phase, subject to the constraints of the Interim Founding Governance Charter.
lessons.title: Section 2. Amendments

lessons.outcome: This specification is adopted under the authority of the OSTF Constitution and the Admiralty Bylaws. It applies to advanced research, modeling, and system architecture within OSTF. Adopted by authority of the OSTF Admiralty.
lessons.title: Article VIII — Adoption

lessons.outcome: Creation, Versioning, Review, and Retirement of OSTF Technical Specifications (SPEC)
lessons.title: SPEC Governance Rulebook

lessons.outcome: This Rulebook is adopted under the **OSTF Constitution**, the **Admiralty Bylaws of OSTF**, the **Ethical AI Usage Policy**, and the **SPEC standards framework**. It governs the lifecycle of OSTF technical specifications, including SPEC-000 through SPEC-006 and all future specifications.
lessons.title: Section 1. Authority

lessons.outcome: This Rulebook ensures that SPEC documents are: 1. Created through a transparent and rigorous process; 2. Versioned, reviewed, and maintained consistently; 3. Aligned with OSTF’s mission, ethics, and security requirements; 4. Retired or superseded in an orderly manner; 5. Traceable in the Alpha State audit system.
lessons.title: Section 2. Purpose

lessons.outcome: OSTF Constitution Admiralty Bylaws of OSTF SPEC-000 (Equity, Accessibility, and Democratization) SPEC-001 (Ethical AI Governance and Rights) SPEC-002 (Technical Standards and Interoperability) SPEC-003 (Code Space and Polyglot Addressing) SPEC-004 (Security Clearance & Classification System) SPEC-005 (Address-as-Ethics Convergence) SPEC-006 (Topological Lattice and Observer Substrate) Ethical AI Usage Policy Research Integrity Policy Corporate Resolution Book Alpha State audit system
lessons.title: Section 3. Related Documents

lessons.outcome: Core SPEC numbers (e.g., SPEC-000, SPEC-001) identify major specifications. Core SPEC numbers are assigned by the SPEC Registry and approved by the Admiralty.
lessons.title: Section 1. Core SPEC Numbers

lessons.outcome: Sub-specifications may be designated with suffixes (e.g., SPEC-001-A, SPEC-002-A). Sub-SPECs extend a core SPEC and are governed by the same lifecycle rules.
lessons.title: Section 2. Sub-SPEC Extensions

lessons.outcome: SPEC numbers may be reserved for planned specifications. Reserved numbers are recorded in the SPEC Registry. Future SPEC numbers are assigned sequentially, with gaps allowed for planned architecture slots.
lessons.title: Section 3. Reserved and Future Numbers

lessons.outcome: Each SPEC has a designated **SPEC Editor** responsible for drafting, maintaining, and coordinating revisions. The Editor is appointed by the Vice Admiral of STEM Initiatives or the Lead Technical Systems Architect.
lessons.title: Section 1. SPEC Editor

lessons.outcome: The **Technical Standards Council** (or equivalent body) advises on SPEC architecture, interoperability, and review. It includes the Vice Admiral of STEM Initiatives, the Lead Security and Fabrication Officer, the Lead Technical Systems Architect, AI Warrant Officers, and invited experts.
lessons.title: Section 2. Technical Standards Council

lessons.outcome: The Commodore of Ethics and Equity, supported by Sheraton under SPEC-001, conducts ethics review for all SPECs that affect AI, data, security, or human rights.
lessons.title: Section 3. Ethics Review

lessons.outcome: The Admiralty retains final authority to approve, amend, or retire SPECs. AI systems do not vote on SPEC governance.
lessons.title: Section 4. Admiralty Authority

lessons.outcome: A new SPEC is proposed by a qualified member through a **SPEC Proposal Document** containing: 1. Proposed number and title; 2. Problem statement and rationale; 3. Relationship to existing SPECs and governance documents; 4. Proposed scope and authority structure; 5. Preliminary ethics and security assessment; 6. Expected implementation impact.
lessons.title: Section 1. Proposal

lessons.outcome: The Technical Standards Council reviews the proposal for: 1. Architectural fit; 2. Need and clarity; 3. Avoidance of duplication; 4. Security and ethics implications.
lessons.title: Section 2. Initial Review

lessons.outcome: If the proposal is accepted, the SPEC Editor drafts the SPEC in the standard format. Drafts are circulated for comment and may be reviewed by AI agents (Sheraton, Digit) in an advisory capacity.
lessons.title: Section 3. Drafting

lessons.outcome: New core SPECs require approval by the Admiralty as follows: Standard SPECs: 3/5 vote; SPECs affecting security, ethics, or AI governance: 4/5 vote; SPECs that modify the governance of SPEC itself or the Real Illumination Covenant: 5/5 unanimous vote. Approval is recorded in the Corporate Resolution Book and the SPEC Registry.
lessons.title: Section 4. Approval

lessons.outcome: Each SPEC shall include: 1. Header with title, number, and adoption status; 2. Article I — Purpose and Authority; 3. Article II — Definitions (if needed); 4. Subsequent articles with operative provisions; 5. Article on Governance and Amendments; 6. Article on Adoption and certification signatures.
lessons.title: Section 1. Standard Structure

lessons.outcome: SPECs must reference related documents, including the Constitution, Admiralty Bylaws, other SPECs, and policies. Cross-references ensure consistency and avoid conflicts.
lessons.title: Section 2. Cross-References

lessons.outcome: Each SPEC must contain clear, enforceable provisions. Avoid vague language. Define roles, thresholds, error conditions, and escalation paths.
lessons.title: Section 3. Operative Provisions

lessons.outcome: SPEC versions use the format **MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH** (e.g., 1.2.0): MAJOR** — incompatible or significant normative change; MINOR** — additive or clarifying change that remains compatible; PATCH** — editorial or typographical correction.
lessons.title: Section 1. Version Numbers

lessons.outcome: Patch** revisions may be approved by the SPEC Editor and recorded in the SPEC Registry. Minor** revisions require approval by the Technical Standards Council and notification to the Admiralty. Major** revisions require Admiralty approval using the same thresholds as new SPECs.
lessons.title: Section 2. Version Approval

lessons.outcome: Each SPEC shall maintain a version history section documenting changes, dates, and approving authority.
lessons.title: Section 3. Version History

lessons.outcome: The Technical Standards Council shall review each active SPEC at least annually for relevance, accuracy, and alignment with technology, security, and ethics developments.
lessons.title: Section 1. Annual Review

lessons.outcome: A SPEC shall be reviewed promptly upon: 1. A significant security incident or vulnerability; 2. A change in the Constitution, Admiralty Bylaws, or related policies; 3. A request by the Fleet Admiral, the Commodore of Ethics and Equity, or the LSFO; 4. A change in the underlying technology or threat landscape; 5. A proposal for major revision or retirement.
lessons.title: Section 2. Triggered Review

lessons.outcome: The SPEC Editor is responsible for maintaining the SPEC between reviews. Maintenance includes patch updates, clarification, and coordination with stakeholders.
lessons.title: Section 3. Maintenance Responsibility

lessons.outcome: A SPEC may be retired when it is no longer relevant, has been superseded, or is obsolete. Retirement requires: 1. A proposal with rationale; 2. Review by the Technical Standards Council; 3. Approval by the Admiralty by 3/5 vote (4/5 for security or ethics SPECs); 4. Recording in the SPEC Registry and Corporate Resolution Book; 5. Notification to all implementers and stakeholders.
lessons.title: Section 1. Retirement

lessons.outcome: A retired SPEC may be superseded by a new or updated SPEC. The superseding SPEC must reference the retired SPEC and explain the relationship. Superseded SPECs remain archived for historical reference.
lessons.title: Section 2. Supersession

lessons.outcome: Retired SPECs are archived in the organized specs directory, the flat root directory, and the Alpha State audit system. They may not be deleted or altered after retirement.
lessons.title: Section 3. Archival

lessons.outcome: The Technical Standards Council maintains a **SPEC Registry** listing all SPECs, their status (draft, active, deprecated, retired), version, editor, and approval record. The Registry is stored in the Alpha State system and mirrored in the public repository when appropriate.
lessons.title: Section 1. Registry Maintenance

lessons.outcome: The Registry and active SPECs are made publicly available unless a SPEC is classified under SPEC-004. Classified SPECs are accessible only to authorized clearance holders.
lessons.title: Section 2. Public Access

lessons.outcome: OSTF systems and personnel must implement active SPECs relevant to their role and clearance level. Implementation plans and timelines are documented in the Annual Operating Plan.
lessons.title: Section 1. Implementation

lessons.outcome: The AIWO Corps and the Technical Standards Council monitor compliance with SPECs, especially SPEC-004 and SPEC-005. Non-compliance is reported to the LSFO and the Admiralty.
lessons.title: Section 2. Compliance Monitoring

lessons.outcome: Waivers from SPEC requirements may be granted only by the Admiralty for cause and with documented conditions. Waivers involving security or ethics require 4/5 vote and are recorded in the Corporate Resolution Book.
lessons.title: Section 3. Waivers

lessons.outcome: Amendments to this Rulebook require a **5/5 unanimous vote** of the Admiralty due to its foundational role in the SPEC ecosystem. During the founding phase, the Fleet Admiral may amend with Admiralty ratification within seventy-two hours.
lessons.title: Article XI — Amendments to this Rulebook

lessons.outcome: This SPEC Governance Rulebook is adopted under the authority of the OSTF Constitution and the Admiralty Bylaws of OSTF. It applies to all SPEC documents and the governance of the OSTF technical standards ecosystem. Adopted by authority of the OSTF Admiralty.
